title: 1976 AHSME Problem 23
statement: For integers \(k\) and \(n\) such that \(1\le k\lt n,\) let \[ \binom nk=\frac{n!}{k!(n-k)!}. \] Then \(\left(\frac{n-2k-1}{k+1}\right)\binom nk\) is an integer

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text:
for all even values of \(k\) and \(n,\) but not for all \(k\)
and \(n\)

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text:
for all odd values of \(k\) and \(n,\) but not for all \(k\)
and \(n\)

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text:
if \(k=1\) or \(n-1,\) but not for all odd values of \(k\) and
\(n\)

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text:
if \(n\) is divisible by \(k,\) but not for all even values of
\(k\) and \(n\)

solutions.text:
Using \[ \binom n{k+1}=\frac{n-k}{k+1}\binom nk, \] and writing \[ \frac{n-2k-1}{k+1}=\frac{n-k}{k+1}-1, \] the given expression becomes \[ \binom n{k+1}-\binom nk. \] This is an integer for every permitted \(k\) and \(n.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: Try rewriting the expression as a difference of two adjacent binomial coefficients
